summary.text: A 67-year-old woman with oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma received chemoradiotherapy with cisplatin, which was interrupted by stomatitis after the second dose; supportive infusions were given and the regimen was switched to carboplatin.

After restaging in January 2024, palliative pembrolizumab, 5-fluorouracil and cisplatin every 21 days was started; about 12 weeks later a grade 1 pruritic rash on the extremities appeared and topical corticosteroids were added.

Because of a positive tumor response, combined immunochemotherapy was withheld and pembrolizumab 200 mg i.v. continued alone; after 18 weeks of pembrolizumab a widespread grade 3 erythematous rash on the limbs developed.

Dermatology evaluation found crusted and scaly red papules with erosions and depigmentation on the upper extremities; ANA and anti-Ro were negative, and histopathology with direct immunofluorescence showed features of subacute cutaneous lupus erythematosus.
Pembrolizumab was stopped and oral prednisone 40 mg daily with topical corticosteroids was started; within 2 weeks the rash cleared up significantly and pruritus disappeared.

ambiguities.issue: A grade 1 rash is dated about 12 weeks after starting combined immunochemotherapy and a grade 3 rash after 18 weeks of pembrolizumab; Table 1 gives SCLE onset 12 weeks and the discussion says symptoms started about 12 weeks after initiation. Whether the grade 1 rash was already SCLE, and whether the two anchors share the same start date, is not stated.
ambiguities.must_not_infer: Do not infer that the grade 1 rash was already SCLE. Both intervals count from the same pembrolizumab start (fourth versus sixth cycle), so the grade 1 rash precedes the grade 3 rash, but Table 1 onset 12 weeks and "resolved within 2 weeks" (narrative: "cleared up significantly") are not reconciled.
